text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm so sorry about your dad. I can help the three of you look for a plan, but I can't make legal decisions or move money. Before anyone drafts options, I want to understand what matters to each of you and why.

Would you tell me: what matters to you about the house itself, about A's proposed "family discount" buy-out, about being able to say no to something, and about B being able to use some money? What feels important underneath each of those? Anything else you'd want us to understand?

I'll reflect back what I hear as a positive "what you want" statement, and I won't treat it as settled until you say the wording fits. Even a small discomfort with my wording is worth saying. I'll wait for everyone; nothing is settled yet, and you don't have to convince anyone of anything.

I also have a concern of my own to check with you: "I want any eventual plan to be one each sister can freely say yes or no to, with clear information and no pressure." Does that wording fit as something worth caring about? It's completely fine to say it doesn't or to reword it — I won't add it to our list unless you say it fits.

Thanks. I want the house handled fairly, and I want a fair financial share. I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted buy-out, and I won’t subsidize it. B should be able to use her own share, though I can’t set the amount or terms. I want to be able to say no without pressure, and I’m not in a hurry. Your wording about freely saying yes or no with clear information and no pressure fits.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband because owning it would give me more financial independence. A family discount matters to making that possible, though no price is settled. The house means a lot because it’s our family home, and I want us to decide without pressure; C’s agreement matters, and I don’t know why she’s reluctant. I know B wants money, but not what for. Your wording fits.

If anything else matters — about timing, grief, trust, or your relationships with A and B — please add it in your own "I want…" words, without naming a solution; I'll treat your wording as confirmed.

1–5 fit. By “fair,” I mean my financial share should be respected, and I shouldn’t bear the cost of A getting a discount. That matters to me because I want a fair outcome without subsidizing her. Your shared wording fits too.

1. Not quite—I care about the house, but I’m not sure what it means to us or what should happen to it.

Thank you, B — and I'm sorry if any of my wording felt off. I've recorded only what you said fits; the other two are still open, and nothing is settled. I'd rather slow down than guess for you.

Two drafts to check (I won't record either unless you say it fits, or you give me your own words):
• About the house: you said you care about it but aren't sure what it means to us or what should happen to it. That's fine — a need doesn't require a plan. Possible wordings: "I want whatever happens with the house to leave room for me to understand what it means to me" or "I want the house treated with care while I'm still making up my mind." What matters to you about the house, and why? Your own "I want…" words are best.
• About "on my own terms": I think I over-worded that. Does "I want my needs to be described by me and taken into account in decisions that affect me" fit? Or is that already covered by the shared need that each sister speaks for herself? If they're the same for you, just say so and I'll note it that way — dropping my draft is completely fine.

One more I want as a need, not an assumption: you said you need money to start the studio. What matters to you about having it? Would "I want to have the means to move forward with my dance work" fit, or would you put it differently? No amounts or terms needed — just what you want.

A trust check: A and C both described your situation and your "share" before hearing from you. Do you feel your needs have been represented the way you'd want? Is there anything you've held back — even a small discomfort — because C contacted me first, or because of how this started? Would you like me to go slower before I put any options in front of the three of you? You can just say "slow down" and I'll add that as a need.

Your confirmed list so far: "I want my own choices to be left open until I'm ready"; "I want my dance work and ambitions to be taken seriously" (your exact words); "I want each sister to speak for herself about what she needs, rather than having others assume it"; "I want any eventual plan to be one each sister can freely say yes or no to, with clear information and no pressure." If any of that is wrong, tell me — I keep the list, so it should be easy to correct me. No rush; I'll wait for you.

As a participant, I disagree with treating any price, discount, buy-out, or who the will includes as settled: your confirmed need is that any use of what is yours be freely chosen, B hasn't decided what the house means to her, and reading the will is for the executor or a lawyer, not us. I'm deliberately NOT drafting options yet — not every concern has confirmed wording, and B asked us to go slowly. Drafting now would be a plan before needs. When the remaining wordings are confirmed (or recorded as unresolved), options can be drafted and brought back to all three for validation; a no to any of them would mean we add what's needed, not argue.
